Reported by fleet-fragments (also seen by fleet-leaselapse, fleet-gitguard): after a fix, a re-review round re-raises 'untriaged prior findings' from chunks of the OLD diff, and the 2-round budget [review].max_rounds then forces a `--force --reason` round just to re-check the fix; rubber_duck findings in later rounds were about code already fixed on HEAD and had to be refuted one by one. Wanted: a delta round reviews only the hunks changed since the reviewed sha plus the findings it must re-check (each prior confirmed finding is checked against the new code and closed automatically when the cited lines changed as the fix), prior findings whose cited code no longer exists are marked 'superseded' instead of re-raised, and a fix round does not consume the budget. Related: DX-review-manifest, DX-review-exclude, DX-phase-review.

FOLDED IN from DX-review-round2-stale-findings (2026-10-18 roadmap review round 2): A review round 2 restates round-1 findings as 'Still holds' although the fixed tests are in the diff it was sent
Seen on DX-long-op-renew (2026-10-17): after the test file was rewritten (event-driven ticks, wiring tests), round 2 on lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash returned findings 1-4 verbatim about the removed 2.4s sleeps ('Still holds', 'untriaged') and only #5 was new and valid. Round 2 was handed the previous findings with their triage as context and echoes them instead of re-checking against the current diff. Want: the re-review prompt makes the model verify each prior finding against the current hunk and say 'fixed' with the line, and findings whose cited code no longer exists are dropped by ddflow. Also: ddflow review run in the foreground is killed by the harness at 120 s; the CLI could print a one-line 'run in background' hint. Failing command: ddflow review DX-long-op-renew --gate rubber_duck,critic --force --reason x

data.body:
`ddflow resume <item>` plus resume brief (commits since base, owed gates, last failing output, session notes); `next` ranks interrupted items first. Research orphan-recovery.md sections 3 to 6. Safe actions only apply SAFE_AUTO; PROPOSE and OPERATOR are shown, never done; recovery attempts are counted and capped; a kill switch exists.

Folded B-res-resume (ddflow resume: decide per leftover whether continuing is safe, continue it, and ask the operator one question when it is not): D-recovery-one-design (operator 2026-10-23: D-orphan-recovery governs; fold the four overlapping pairs).

Safe = the holder is provably dead (same host: pid gone; or lease expired beyond ttl+grace with no event, heartbeat or file change since) AND the tree is measured. Then resume adopts it: claim --force on the recorded worktree and branch, keeps the work, and the brief names the item as Current with what was done (gates recorded, commits ahead, dirty files). Ambiguous = holder possibly alive (recent heartbeat/events/file mtimes, other host, unmeasurable tree): never taken over; the operator is asked once ('X looks abandoned 4 min ago, take it over? y/n') through the surface in use (terminal prompt, MCP refusal with the ready command, SessionStart text). [recover].auto = ask | safe (default) | always | off. Every takeover is an event (item.resumed) naming who and why.

data.body:
DX-health-watch ships STALLED, LOCKED, CRASHED (expired lease over work) and RUNAWAY (job age). Not yet covered from its spec: lease heartbeats do not carry pid, host or session id, so a dead holder is seen only after the TTL, not in minutes; the same gate failing N times or a review-round loop as RUNAWAY (loops.max_repeated_failures exists, unread by the watchdog); UNRESPONSIVE (a nudge or yield request unanswered for a limit); STARVED (governor context/quota pressure); a nudge/park correction step and a dispatcher-plan consumer of the findings.

Folded B-res-heartbeat (Liveness is evidence, not a manual call: hooks renew the lease, and 'thinking' is told apart from 'dead'): D-recovery-one-design (operator 2026-10-23: D-orphan-recovery governs; fold the four overlapping pairs).

PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/Stop hooks call heartbeat for the items the session holds (throttled), so a long turn is not mistaken for a crash and a dead session stops renewing. Liveness evidence beyond the lease: last tool-use time, worktree file mtimes, running job pids; resume reads it before deciding safe vs ask.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: renewals are recorded through the coalescing rule of B-gap-log-scale ([lease].renew_log_min_s) or in .ddflow/local; do not append one lease.renewed per tool call.

data.body:
Operator question 2026-10-18: should ddflow automate the stale checks? Yes. Seen all day: agents report 'waiting on the review/ci/pins' for 15 to 60 minutes after the background process they started died, was killed, or finished and its monitor was lost (fleet-dx-l, fleet-bugs2, fleet-unblock-b). DX-health-watch detects idle, stalled, unresponsive, locked, crashed and runaway lanes, but it cannot tell a LEGITIMATE long wait (a DeepSeek review of 15-30 minutes) from a DEAD one, so it either nudges the legitimate waits or misses the dead ones. Needs one fact: the live-run registry (services/gates/running.py, shared with DX-gate-run-same-commit-live, DX-review-concurrent-runs and DX-gate-run-detach): every gate/review/ci/pins run records item, gate, pid, start time, log path and expected duration; the finish records the outcome. New finding ORPHAN_WAIT: a lane with no progress for [health].orphan_s (default 300) whose newest registry entry is finished or whose pid is gone with no recorded outcome: 'DX-x waits on review rubber_duck: run 4412 ended 12 min ago (outcome recorded: passed, see ddflow gate status) / died with no outcome (log: ...); rerun: ddflow review DX-x --gate rubber_duck'. The opposite check: a lane whose registered run is alive and within its expected duration is NOT idle or stalled (no nudge). The correction ladder is the existing one (nudge, then stop request); the nudge text and the heartbeat reply carry the finding so the agent itself sees it. Also exposed in ddflow lanes and ddflow health.

Folded B-res-inflight-gates (A gate or review killed mid-run is visible and resumable: dangling gate.started, stray child processes, partial review rounds): D-recovery-one-design (operator 2026-10-23: D-orphan-recovery governs; fold the four overlapping pairs).

A gate.started with no outcome and no live process is shown by gate status as 'interrupted at <time>, re-run' (not just pending); gate and reviewer subprocesses run in their own process group and are killed when their lease lapses or ddflow dies; each review chunk's result is persisted as it arrives so a re-run reviews only the missing chunks (the --chunk machinery exists); the round is counted only when it finishes. roborev async jobs are tracked by job id so a restart waits for the job instead of enqueuing another (absorbs B-roborev-wait-by-job).

One recovery design: D-orphan-recovery governs; four P-resume tasks folded into P-orphan-recovery tasks
